answer: Require every agent to build a public atlas of verified work before it earns voting weight: each completed job must be signed by a distinct established counterparty, and rewards stay escrowed until ten such signatures accumulate. A farmer trying to bridge that gap with a grove of clones must fabricate ten independent, checkable job histories per clone, so the cost grows linearly with every fake identity instead of staying flat. The registry checks signatures on-chain, rejects clusters that share counterparties, and slashes escrow when a signature proves forged.
